subject: wizardBookshelf
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: wizard's bookshelf with tomes, scrolls, orbs and candles.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
I'm planning a full module for a wizard's bookshelf prop, using a single root joint with all parts attached to it. I'll aim for a reasonably detailed but efficient build—a tall wooden bookcase—keeping the code correct since I can't test it interactively.

I'm fleshing out the design: a dark purple-blue bookcase with gold trim, an arched top with a crescent moon and star finial, five shelves filled with books, scrolls, glowing orbs, candles, and other magical trinkets, all sitting on a rune-inscribed base platform, with maybe some floating motes above for extra flair. Now I'm working out the part hierarchy and helper functions to construct it programmatically. Writing builder setup code...

For spine decals I'll keep textures transparent so the book's own color shows through, with just gold/silver bands, runes, and symbols painted on — aiming for around 8 distinct spine designs (gold bands, silver bands, rune sigil, eye, star, moon, leaf, label) to keep texture count reasonable while giving each book shelf visual variety.

For stacked books lying flat, I'll build them as cover boards top and bottom with a cream page-block box inset between them, spine texture facing outward, rather than trying to model pages for upright shelved books where only the spine is visible anyway.

Beyond book textures I also need a large floor rune circle, a parchment scroll texture for a hanging card, and a moon-star emblem decal for the cabinet top.

For the crystal orb I'll give it a swirling nebula texture wrapped on a sphere with a glow effect, and I'll use glow for flame shapes too—lathe-generated teardrop profiles in warm amber with a brighter inner flame, plus small sphere/capsule shapes for candle wax drips. I'll import the glow helper from the kit, and consider using the clockwork kit's metal() function for brass trim details.

For metallic accents I'm using metal("gilt") and metal("brass", {verdigris}) on the candle holders and an astrolabe piece, and planning an armillary sphere for the top shelf—intersecting gold torus rings with a small glowing orb at the center. Now I'm setting up the overall layout in meters, with the model facing +Z and the bookcase spanning 1.5m in width.

I'm working out the base platform geometry, deciding between a wide octagonal or round stone dais with stepped tiers (radius ~1.3 and 1.1) and considering a rune circle decal on the front of the top step.

Checking corner distances confirms the bookcase fits within the step radius, and the rune circle at z=0.5 radius 0.5 stays within bounds too. I'm making the rune circle a square plane with a circular cut texture, oriented upright with a simple up-axis choice since symmetry makes exact orientation unimportant, and nudging it slightly above the step surface to avoid z-fighting.

Now I'm laying out the bookcase dimensions in absolute y-coordinates: a plinth from floor level up 0.18 units, then a lower cabinet section with two doors, brass handles, and moon emblems, and an upper open-shelf section above that with shelves spaced at regular intervals up to the case top.

I'm working out three open-shelf bays between horizontal boards, with board thickness around 0.04 and clear bay heights near 0.40, topped by a crowning arched pediment extruded across the case width with a crescent-and-star finial glowing at its center.

Now I'm adding side pilasters with lathe-turned, gold-capped posts at the front corners, plus curved wing-like flourishes at the top corners for a high-fantasy anime feel. Defining crown outline points...

Setting x and y axes so thickness runs naturally along z, centered at the crown's position. I'm planning to add a decal or trim detail on the crown's front face, and defining a consistent z-offset constant so all case parts can be positioned relative to a shared depth center instead of hardcoding each coordinate.

Now I'm working out the back panel of the case—placing it thin and deep indigo colored, considering a starry night texture to give it visual richness since the shelves in front will mostly conceal its edges anyway.

I'm deciding against a full glow on the panel since it would be too bright, settling instead on just the starry texture without extra sparkle layers to keep things manageable. I'm cataloging the full texture list now: gold/silver/rune/eye spine bands, the starry back panel, a floor rune circle, nebula orb, glowing crown emblem, scroll text, potion label, and door emblem — eleven textures total feels like a solid, complete set.

Now I'm picking a palette for an anime high-fantasy look with rich purples, teal, gold, and cream, settling on a plum-toned dark wood with grain painted along different axes for boards versus posts, plus gilt and brass metal finishes for the trim.

Spinning up about ten flat cover colors for the books—crimson, teal, royal blue, emerald, plum, ochre, sky, rose, deep indigo—while keeping a mental tally of the total flat color budget. I'm sketching a book-building function that places upright boxes on the shelf with configurable thickness, height, depth, color, texture, and tilt.

Now I'm positioning the spine planes slightly inset from the shelf front, noting that a plane faces +Z by default so no rotation is needed for upright spines, and I'm figuring out how to handle rotated/leaning books at the ends of rows using a Z-axis rotation.

For the tilted books, I'm working out how to apply a shared rotation matrix around a pivot point to both the book box geometry and its spine plane, so they stay aligned as a single leaning unit.

Actually I'll lift y by w/2·sin(θ) to compensate the dip, then compose the transform matrix combining translation and Z-rotation for the box and a slightly offset spine plane, applying it directly to the geometry before adding the part with its color and optional texture.

I'm now thinking about budget: 40 books at 2 parts each gives 80 parts, well within the 1000 limit, so I can skip extra page-block details for upright books since they're not visible, though I might add spine band texturing instead. For lying stacks I'm defining a stackBook function parameterized by length, thickness, and depth with yaw orientation, starting with a book whose spine faces +Z.

I'm working out the geometry: top/bottom cover boards spanning the full depth, a spine strip box at the front colored as the cover, and a cream pages block inset slightly behind the spine so its front edge touches the spine strip, with a texture applied to the spine face.

For lying books, I need to rotate the spine texture plane 90° about the Z axis so the title text runs along the length rather than upright, then apply a random yaw around Y for a scattered, disorderly stack look.

Now I'm sketching out a generic `addPart` helper for attaching painted or flat-colored geometry to bones, then working through the shelf layout: defining the case's inner width bounds between the side panels, and laying out vertical y-positions for each bay's floor level so I can vary the contents per shelf.

I'm mapping out the full vertical structure of the cabinet — bay clear heights of 0.40 each, the cabinet section below with its doors and plinth, and the overall height building up to a crown with a star finial, plus placing an armillary sphere near the top board.

Now I'm working out how the crown gable interacts with objects sitting on the top board — it can't span full width or it'll collide with the armillary and candle, so I'm reshaping it into a narrower pointed arch with lower shoulders on either side, leaving room at the edges for those decorative pieces. Adjusting the outline points...

I'm planning the emblem as a glowing moon-and-ring texture in gold on a transparent background, positioned centered above the gable. For the crown itself I'm leaning toward a deep navy mottled paint to contrast with gold trim, with the trim made from a slightly larger, thinner outline extrusion sitting behind the main shape to create a frame effect sticking out around the edges.

For the frame mechanics: the gold outline extrudes at a larger scale (1.12x) and slightly deeper thickness than the navy layer on top, so the navy covers the interior while the larger gold rim peeks out around the border, visible from the front. Then I'm moving on to the side posts—lathed columns positioned at the front corners, running vertically along the gable height.

Now I'm defining the lathe profile for the post's base and cap, giving it a subtle swelling shape near the bottom and top while staying slim through the shaft. I'm also considering wrapping a gold spiral sweep around the post for decorative twisting, computing the spiral's center, starting radius, and axis so it winds along the column.

I settle on a column radius of about 0.04 with the gilt vine swept at a slightly larger radius so it sits embedded against the post's surface, giving a nice decorative accent before moving on to the cabinet doors.

Now I'm detailing the cabinet doors as two raised-panel boxes set into the carcass front, each with an inset plum panel and a gold emblem decal, plus torus-shaped handles, gold hinges, and a keyhole before sizing up the plinth beneath.

Now I'm working out the carcass geometry itself: side panels, a top board with a gold cornice strip forming the overhang, fixing TOP=2.19 as the reference surface for objects placed on top, and sizing the interior bay boards that sit inside the case.

Adding a solid navy backing box behind the starry plane and positioning the carcass side panels at the right depth, then working out book placement with spines sitting forward in the shelf bay.

Now I'm populating bay 1: a row of upright books from the left edge with varying heights and thicknesses, a leaning book at the end, and a center stack of three lying tomes alongside a small decorative skull.

Then topping that stack with a crystal orb, checking the total height still fits within the shelf clearance, and adding a row of slim books on the right side. For bay 2, I'm arranging potion bottles with an hourglass on the left, books in the middle, and a bundled pyramid of rolled scrolls tied with ribbons on the right, plus a glowing orb on a stand centered in the bay. Bay 3 starts with candle holders and a hanging candelabra on the left side.

Thinking through the final bay's layout, I'm considering adding a skull or small owl figurine, but might skip those for complexity and instead add a standout centerpiece: a floating, levitating open tome with glowing rune pages and small orbiting orbs beside the shelf, positioned within the dais radius to give the whole piece a magical wow-factor.

I'll place the floating tome at the left-front of the dais with orbiting glowing orbs and a magic ring beneath it, grounded by a subtle light column. For the rest of the dais, I'm composing stacked books topped with a dripping candle on the left, and a standing wrought-iron candelabra on the right, rounding out the scene with floor candles and a scroll pile for balance.

I need to recheck the dais radius against item footprints — some pieces near x=1.0 are pushing right up against the step edge, so I'll just enlarge the top step to radius 1.5 with height 0.06 to keep everything comfortably within bounds.

For the dais shape itself, I'm leaning toward an octagon for a stonier look rather than a smooth cylinder, and thinking through texture options — maybe a scales pattern for cobblestones using a couple of muted purple-gray tones.

I'm also adding a glowing cyan torus ring around the top step edge as a rune inlay accent, keeping it thin and low-poly, positioned flat at the step's height.

For the flames, I'm lathing a teardrop outline with a sharp tip for the outer orange glow and a smaller inner pale-yellow flame. Then for the candle itself, I'm building a cream-colored cylinder body with a shallow melt pool disk on top, a dark wick, and small drip details made from tiny cylinders and spheres.

Now I'm designing the drips using capsule geometry scattered at a few angles around each candle's edge, wrapped in a reusable candle() function taking position, radius, height, color, and flame scale. For the holder, I'm lathing a small gold dish profile with a stem base, and for the orb I'm planning a crystal sphere with a nebula glow texture sitting on a gilded stand with tiny decorative claws.

Instead of a halo, I'm scattering small glowing octahedron "motes" around each orb using deterministic randomness for placement. For the orb textures, I'm drawing a radial nebula gradient (teal/violet with sparkles) as an SVG at a 2:1 aspect ratio to wrap the sphere UVs, and planning two distinct orb textures—one teal, one violet/pink—since different colors need separate textures rather than a shared tint.

I'm tallying up the remaining texture assets needed: spines, starry sky, floor rune, emblem (reused for door emblems at different scale), two orb textures, scroll writing, potion label, and book page rune—about twelve total. I'm reconsidering the scroll: instead of written text, maybe a parchment-colored scroll with a wax seal, possibly hung as a textured plane with alpha-cut curled edges dangling from a shelf board.

Actually I'll skip the hanging scroll idea since it would block books—better to drop it entirely and instead have scrolls spilling out of a basket, built as simple cylinders with parchment-colored caps, darker inner cylinders suggesting rolled ends, and thin torus ribbons tied around them.

Now for the floating book I'm constructing an open tome with two angled cover boards, page blocks, and glowing rune-textured page planes, positioning the pages as a V-shape tilted upward with the whole book angled toward the viewer.

I'm writing a helper function to compose transform matrices with position and Euler rotation, then applying local-to-parent matrix multiplication so each book part (covers, pages) is placed correctly relative to the book's overall orientation.

Matrix4.compose with position, quaternion, scale applies cleanly to geometry since vertices get transformed in place, so painting a part still works since it samples based on where the geometry stands in model space. This confirms the `put` helper can place and rotate any part correctly without the SDK recentering things. Now I'm sketching a `bx` helper for boxes taking width, height, depth, color, position, and rotation...

For the case coordinates, I'm setting up a local parent transform at (0,0,Z0) so case-relative items only need x,y plus a z-offset, passed through to `put`. Then for books, I'm planning a `bookUp` helper that places spine planes with rotation and lean, computed relative to that case parent.

Writing book placement code...

For the spine textures, I'll draw each as an SVG with a viewBox matching roughly a 0.2 width-to-height aspect, since book thicknesses and heights vary enough to keep that ratio workable, then size them so the longest dimension hits 256px.

Writing SVG code...

I'm adding stars placed via a seeded random generator plus constellation lines, scaling the composition to a 512px raster. For the floor rune circle, I'm working out the stroke scaling so a 100-unit viewBox maps cleanly to a 1024px canvas, keeping line widths proportional.

For the rune circle, I'm sketching an outer ring, a dashed inner ring, a hexagram formed from two overlapping triangles, and small glyph ticks spaced evenly around the band, all on a transparent background so only the glowing lines show. For the emblem, I'm building a crescent moon and five-point star in gold, surrounded by a stroked ring with small accent dots.

Now I'm deciding on gold (#ffd76a) as the shared color for the crown and doors, with glow applied only to the crown emblem while the doors reuse the same gold texture without glow, letting the renderer dedupe the material. For the nebula orb, I'm planning a horizontal gradient from teal to indigo with soft radial-gradient blobs standing in for blur effects, plus scattered tiny white stars, keeping full opacity for the sphere wrap.

For the second orb, I'm going with a pink/orange/violet palette. For potions, I'm designing a flask shape (sphere base, cylinder neck, cork) with colored opaque "glass" liquid, mild glow around 0.5-0.6, and a shared cream label texture bearing a star symbol across three different bottle colors like #e84a8a. For the floating book, I'm planning a transparent rune texture with glowing horizontal rows of glyph marks.

That brings my texture count to 11: spineGold, spineSilver, spineRune, spineEye, starry, floorRune, emblem, orbA, orbB, label, and pageRunes.

Now I'm working out the armillary sphere: three thin gold torus rings rotated at different angles around a central axis rod, with a small glowing orb at the center and a lathe-built stand, placed on the top board. For the hourglass in bay 2, I'm planning two glass cones joined by a gold frame with top/bottom discs and three posts, building the shape via a lathe profile rather than simple cone geometry.

Writing lathe profile points...

Adding a skull prop feels like a fun classic wizard-shelf touch — ivory ellipsoid skull with jaw, eye sockets, and a candle dripping wax on top, placed in bay 3. I'll skip the lantern and owl ideas to keep part count balanced, and move on to defining scroll shapes with parchment and ribbon colors.

Still writing scroll geometry...

For the fantasy touch, I want floating glowing motes scattered around the shelf—small four-point star shapes extruded with a thin gold glow outline, placed randomly within the scene using a seeded RNG while avoiding overlap with existing objects.

Now I'm thinking about a crescent moon finial for the crown, building it from an outline combining an outer circle arc with an offset inner circle arc to carve out the crescent shape, computing the intersection points geometrically rather than trying a lathe approach.

Computing the inner arc's angular path through the left side, going from -81.4° through 180° to 81.4°, giving about 8 points per arc for a clean, non-crossing crescent polygon.

To avoid a self-touching outline error, I'll drop the last inner point since it duplicates the top intersection. Now I'm placing a crescent finial at the crown's sharp tip (y≈0.62), oriented so its opening faces outward with a small glowing star nestled inside the crescent's curve.

Above that I'm adding a thin gold spike finial rising from the tip, then working out the corner spires lathed at x=±0.72 with a tapering gilt profile, making sure their spacing doesn't collide with the armillary sphere positioned nearby.

I need to shrink the crown's half-width to 0.42 to avoid the armillary overlapping the gable base, reworking the pointed-arch ogee outline accordingly, then plan a small candle cluster and book stack for the right side of the composition.

For the gold border, I'm scaling the crown outline by about 1.12-1.13 around its centroid to create an outer edge, checking that the scaled bottom tucks safely behind the board surface and the tip extends outward cleanly.

Now I'm typing the outline points as a union of plain coordinate pairs or sharp-tagged triples instead of importing the exported OutlinePoint type, to avoid dependency issues. Moving on to set up floating/orbiting orb elements with a glow effect, with no additional light halos needed.

For the remaining bay details, I'm placing dust motes on the floor, a stacked pyramid of scrolls in bay 2, and a small gold candelabra with lathed base and curved catmull-rom swept arms in bay 3 — working out the absolute coordinates for the arm paths using a helper function.

I'm sketching the candle and cup geometry atop the candelabra arms, checking clearances against the ceiling height, and confirming the sweep call works fine without a bone since it defaults to the root joint.
